questions.q: Otilio Arellano gained international acclaim for designing the Philippine Pavilion at the 1958 World's Fair in Brussels. What was the unique 'salakot-inspired' feature of this design?
o: A massive concrete dome painted gold
A wide-brimmed, sweeping roofline reminiscent of a traditional hat
A series of interconnected nipa huts
A skyscraper shaped like a bamboo shoot
questions.n: This 'Neo-Vernacular' approach used the shape of the salakot to represent Filipino identity on a modern global stage.

questions.q: Which prominent government building in Intramuros, standing on the site of the former Spanish Governor-General's residence, was designed by Otilio Arellano?
questions.n: Otilio designed this modern office building in Intramuros, which currently houses the COMELEC and other government agencies.

questions.q: Otilio Arellano was a pioneer in 'Neo-Vernacular' architecture. What does this term primarily refer to?
o: Building only with mud and straw
Destroying all old buildings to build glass boxes
Using modern materials to reinterpret traditional and indigenous Filipino forms
questions.n: Otilio sought to create a 'Filipino' modernism by looking at local motifs like the bahay kubo and traditional crafts.

questions.q: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Main Building along Taft Avenue is a notable work by Otilio. Which architectural style does it best represent?
questions.n: The building features the typical sun-shading fins and blocky geometry of the 1950s and 60s Philippine modern style.

questions.q: Otilio Arellano was the son of which other famous Filipino architect?
questions.n: Arcadio, the elder of the Arellano brothers, was Otilio's father.

questions.q: Otilio Arellano's 1958 Brussels World's Fair Pavilion was noted for its use of which architectural concept to express Filipino identity?
questions.n: This approach reinterprets traditional forms, like the salakot hat, using contemporary materials and engineering.

questions.q: The Palacio del Gobernador in Intramuros was a post-war reconstruction. How did Otilio's design differ from the original Spanish-era structure?
o: It was designed as a hollow ruin to commemorate the war
It utilized a high-rise office block format with modern amenities
It was built entirely of timber and bamboo
It followed strict Neoclassical orders with Ionic columns
questions.n: The design replaced the low-slung colonial palace with a multi-story functional office building suitable for modern bureaucracy.

questions.q: Which of these features on the NBI Building demonstrates Otilio's adaptation of the International Style for the Philippine climate?
o: Thick stone walls with no windows
questions.n: These 'sun-breakers' allowed for large windows while protecting the interior from direct solar heat.

questions.q: In the 1960s, Otilio Arellano was part of a movement that sought to create a 'Filipino' style. This was a reaction against which global trend?
o: The cookie-cutter uniformity of the International Style
questions.n: Architects like Otilio felt that modernism should reflect local culture rather than looking the same in every country.

questions.q: True or False: Otilio Arellano's work is considered a bridge between the 'Grand Classicism' of the early 1900s and the 'Tropical Modernism' of the 1960s and 70s.
questions.n: His career spanned the post-war era where he translated his family's artistic legacy into modern structural languages.

questions.q: The 'Salakot' roof of the 1958 Pavilion was not just symbolic; it also served what practical architectural function?
o: Storing electrical batteries for the fair
Acting as a giant rainwater collection tank
Providing massive shade and promoting natural air updrafts
Serving as a landing pad for helicopters
questions.n: The sweeping roof protected the glass walls from the sun and allowed hot air to rise and escape.

questions.q: Which of these materials would you most likely find in an Otilio Arellano project from the 1950s, signifying its 'Modern' status?
o: Exposed steel beams and large glass panes
Hand-carved narra panels in the Baroque style
questions.n: These materials defined the transparency and structural honesty of the mid-century modern era.

questions.q: Otilio Arellano was awarded the 'Patnubay ng Sining at Kalinangan' by the City of Manila. This award is typically given to those who:
o: Have made outstanding contributions to the city's culture and arts
Have never had a building demolished
Are the youngest licensed architects in the country
Have the highest number of buildings constructed
questions.n: This prestigious award recognized Otilio's role in defining Manila's post-war identity.

questions.q: The NBI Building's location on Taft Avenue places it among many other historic structures. How did Otilio's design respect its urban context?
o: By using bright neon lights on the facade
By mimicking the neoclassical columns of the nearby PGH
By being the tallest building in the world at the time
By maintaining a civic scale and formal presence
questions.n: The building's symmetrical and orderly facade preserved the 'institutional' feel of Taft Avenue while using a modern vocabulary.

questions.q: True or False: Otilio Arellano was part of the 'Arellano and Associates' firm which continued the professional practice established by his father.
questions.n: The firm was a vehicle for the family's continued influence on Philippine architecture across several decades.
